items.headline: Government takes possession of Lee Kuan Yew’s 38 Oxley Road home
items.summary: The Singapore Land Authority and National Heritage Board completed the compulsory acquisition of 38 Oxley Road on 31 July, ending a decade-long Lee-family dispute; NHB will study turning the house into a public heritage space. Lee Hsien Yang called the move a disregard of his late father’s wish to have it demolished.

items.headline: Four new Cross Island Line MRT stations announced for Singapore’s west
items.summary: Transport Minister Jeffrey Siow announced on 31 July that four stations will make up Cross Island Line Phase 3, serving Taman Jurong residents and western industrial-estate workers, with completion targeted for the late 2030s.

items.headline: Singapore tightens driver demerit-point limits after road deaths hit a 10-year high
items.summary: From 1 January 2027 the licence-suspension threshold for non-probationary drivers falls from 24 to 18 demerit points, after road fatalities rose about 5% to 149 in 2025, a 10-year high; the Safe Driving Course that let drivers cut points will be scrapped.

items.headline: Singaporeans among 65 arrested in Vietnam over an etomidate-laced vape syndicate
items.summary: Ho Chi Minh City police charged 65 people, including four Singaporeans, over an etomidate-vape ring and seized 1,331 pods; Singaporean Melvin Tan Junjie, 30, is named a ringleader, while a missing Singaporean allegedly supplied the liquid.

items.headline: Beauty chain DNA Brands to refund up to S$1 million over high-pressure sales
items.summary: The Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore secured a commitment of up to S$1 million in refunds from DNA Brands after finding staff kept customers in treatment rooms to pressure purchases since 2023; CASE will administer refunds for buyers from 1 January 2023.

items.headline: India’s GST collections jump 15.4% to a record Rs 2.11 lakh crore in July
items.summary: Gross GST revenue rose 15.4% year-on-year to Rs 2.11 lakh crore in July, as import-linked revenue surged 28.8% to Rs 66,511 crore and domestic collections grew 10.1%; net revenue after refunds rose 15.8% to Rs 1.81 lakh crore.

items.headline: Modi launches South India’s first chip plant near Visakhapatnam
items.summary: Prime Minister Modi inaugurated an outsourced semiconductor assembly-and-test (OSAT) plant at Tarluvada, Andhra Pradesh, built with South Korea’s APACT as technology partner, that will package and test chips for AI, data centres and high-speed communications.

items.headline: NIA court frames charges against ex-officers Waze and Sharma in Antilia bomb-scare case
items.summary: A special NIA court framed charges under the anti-terror UAPA against former Mumbai police officers Sachin Waze and Pradeep Sharma in the Antilia explosives-scare and Mansukh Hiran murder case, clearing the way for trial.

items.headline: Amit Shah approves Rs 2,117 crore advance disaster-fund release for flood-hit states
items.summary: The Union Home Ministry approved Rs 2,117.85 crore in advance State Disaster Response Fund money for monsoon-hit states, with immediate tranches to Himachal Pradesh and Odisha and central teams assessing damage in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam.

items.headline: India’s first-quarter fiscal deficit widens to Rs 3.1 lakh crore, 18.2% of the annual target
items.summary: Controller General of Accounts data showed the April-June fiscal gap at Rs 3.07 lakh crore, or 18.2% of the Rs 16.96 lakh crore full-year target, up from a year earlier, even as capital spending rose to Rs 3.4 lakh crore.

Regular coverage resumes tomorrow.

items.headline: Update: US and Israel ready strikes on Iran’s power grid as Tehran vows to hit energy sites
items.summary: US and Israeli forces are preparing a large-scale campaign against Iran’s energy infrastructure that reporting says could cut electricity to Tehran, with President Trump withholding the final order; Iran’s wartime command chief warned Washington is fanning a full-scale regional war and threatened to strike US and Israeli infrastructure.

items.headline: Update: Israel rejects a Gaza pullout as the world reacts to the Hamas disarmament roadmap
items.summary: A day after the US-led Board of Peace announced a staged Hamas disarmament deal, Israel signalled it will not withdraw from Gaza until the Strip is fully demilitarised, with minister Itamar Ben-Gvir calling the plan unacceptable; Palestinians and others objected that it sidelines the United Nations.

items.headline: Car bomb wounds at least 11 in Colombia’s Cúcuta days before a new president takes office
items.summary: A car bomb detonated in Cúcuta on the Venezuela border, wounding at least 11 people, six days before right-wing President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella is due to succeed outgoing leftist President Gustavo Petro; no group claimed responsibility.

items.headline: Human Rights Watch says Russia’s Africa Corps killed Malian civilians in a June air strike
items.summary: A Human Rights Watch report says a Sukhoi jet dropped munitions on the village of Kyrnia, Mali, in June, with one strike near the village chief’s home killing his wife, two children and others; Russian paramilitaries have fought alongside Mali’s junta since 2021.

items.headline: Voice-AI startup Smallest.ai raises $13 million for ultra-fast conversational models
items.summary: Smallest.ai raised a $13 million Series A led by Seligman Ventures, with Sierra Ventures and 3one4 Capital, pushing total funding past $21 million, on a bet that smaller specialised models beat large ones for real-time voice agents.

items.headline: Repeat founder Ryan Williams raises $10 million for AI agents in private credit
items.summary: Ellis AI emerged from stealth with a $10 million seed from First Round, 645 Ventures, Khosla and Thrive, plus Ariel’s Mellody Hobson, to run AI agents across the documents and correspondence that private-credit managers handle.

items.headline: US Treasury yields spike to an 18-month high even as Wall Street closes July with a gain
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 4.737% on Friday, its highest since January 2025, and the 30-year neared 5.22%, yet stocks still rose: the Dow added 276.97 points (0.53%) to 52,485, the S&P 500 gained 0.7% and the Nasdaq rose 1%.

items.headline: Equinix seeks at least $3 billion in bonds to fund AI data-centre expansion
items.summary: Data-centre operator Equinix launched a US investment-grade bond sale of at least $3 billion to finance capacity expansion driven by surging demand for AI computing power.

items.headline: 🎾 Eala routs Osaka to reach her first WTA 500 final, meeting Pegula in Washington
items.summary: Alexandra Eala beat Naomi Osaka 6-4, 6-2 in the DC Open semifinals to reach the biggest final of her career, and faces top seed Jessica Pegula, who downed Diana Shnaider 7-5, 6-4; Pegula leads their head-to-head 1-0.

items.headline: 🎾 The Canadian Open gets under way in Montreal and Toronto
items.summary: The National Bank Open, a Masters 1000 and WTA 1000 hard-court event, began its run from 1 to 13 August, with the men in Montreal and the women in Toronto in the last big tune-up before the US Open.

items.headline: 🏏 The Hundred: Welsh Fire beat Birmingham Phoenix; Southern Brave down London Spirit
items.summary: In the men’s competition on 1 August, Welsh Fire chased 138 to win by seven wickets at Edgbaston, while Southern Brave bowled out London Spirit for 105 and won by five wickets at Lord’s.

items.headline: 🏎️ F1’s summer break rolls on with the Dutch GP next as silly season swirls
items.summary: With no race this weekend, Formula 1 remains in its summer shutdown; the next round is the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort on 21-23 August, a sprint weekend, while paddock talk centres on Max Verstappen’s future and Red Bull’s 2027 line-up.

fun_fact.headline: The pistol shrimp stuns prey with a bubble nearly as hot as the Sun
fun_fact.body: The pistol shrimp hunts with sound. It snaps a specialised claw shut so fast that it fires a bubble of water at its prey; as that bubble collapses it briefly reaches thousands of degrees — close to the temperature of the surface of the Sun — and gives off a faint flash of light. The snap is also one of the loudest sounds in the ocean, loud enough to stun or kill small fish.

puzzle.title: Fair Exchange
puzzle.body:
You have two identical glasses. One holds exactly 500 ml of wine, the other exactly 500 ml of water.
You take one tablespoon (15 ml) of wine from the wine glass and stir it into the water glass.
You then take one tablespoon of the now-mixed liquid from the water glass and stir it back into the wine glass.
Is there now more water in the wine glass, or more wine in the water glass — or are the two amounts equal?
puzzle.approach: Track what leaves each glass and what replaces it, and remember both glasses end at the same volume they started with.
puzzle.answer:
The two amounts are exactly equal.

After the two transfers, each glass again holds 500 ml (a tablespoon left the wine glass and a tablespoon came back). Since the wine glass is back to its original volume, whatever wine is now missing from it must have been replaced by an equal volume of water. That missing wine is precisely the wine sitting in the water glass. So the water in the wine glass and the wine in the water glass are the same amount — no matter how well or badly you stirred, and whatever the spoon size.

word_puzzle.title: Sea to Sky
word_puzzle.body:
Turn SEA into SKY in three steps.
Change exactly one letter at each step, and every rung must be a real English word.

SEA → _ _ _ → _ _ _ → SKY
word_puzzle.approach: Change one letter at a time, keeping every rung a real English word, and let the middle letters do the work before the ends.
word_puzzle.answer:
SEA → SPA → SPY → SKY

SEA → SPA (change E to P)
SPA → SPY (change A to Y)
SPY → SKY (change P to K)
Three steps, each a valid word.
